name: Belagavi
headline: Child marriage and sugarcane-economy pressure sit behind adolescent exits, even as results stay strong.
summary: Belagavi coverage centres on child marriage, with a minor married twice and the Akka Pade task force stopping marriages, and on child-labour rescues from local businesses. Sugarcane price disputes are reported as background to household stress, though no source links them to dropout. The division records a 95.71% SSLC pass rate in 2026. Belagavi Chikkodi was not researched separately.

reasons.detail: A 15-year-old was married off twice before the legal age, and the Akka Pade task force has intercepted marriages and sent girls to child protection committees.
Authorities rescued five school-age children from a bakery, one of several raids on commercial establishments.
About 100 Maharashtra families bring children to cut cane in Belagavi for four to five months; the growers' association reported about 50 young children up to Class 5 lacking schooling.
Prolonged farmer protests over cane prices signal income instability in agricultural households, though the sources do not tie it to dropout directly.

A fact-finding report described 20 Adivasi migrant workers, including nine children, in debt-tied cane work in Belagavi; district authorities reportedly found no child labour. Schooling was not discussed.
For Marathi-speaking cutter children, the education department proposed tent schools near cane fields with Marathi teachers, implying existing Kannada-medium provision was not reaching them.
Belagavi educational district recorded a 2024-25 SSLC pass rate below the prior year, which raises exam-related exit risk; the source does not tie this to dropout counts.
A 2016 CRY-partnered study of child brides across six districts including Belgaum found most were Class 10 dropouts and many faced distance barriers; no Belagavi-only breakdown was given.

gaps: No district dropout, out-of-school or Class 8-10 retention figures; the SSLC figure is for the whole division; Chikkodi sub-area not covered. No Belagavi or Chikkodi dropout counts, UDISE+ figures, Class 8-10 exit surveys or Athani/Raibag-specific reporting retrieved; Deccan Herald pages blocked fetching, so its figures rest on search snippets. Evidence is mostly primary-age migration.
verificationNotes: All kept figures and attributions were confirmed on the cited pages.

entries.factor: % Population Living in Households with Improved Sanitation
entries.why: Belagavi includes rural areas where household sanitation may be poor. No district-specific source links sanitation to dropouts, but lack of toilets can cause illness and girls to miss school, contributing to dropout risk.
entries.mechanism: Poor sanitation -> health and hygiene issues -> absenteeism -> dropout (general).

entries.factor: % Population Living in Households with Improved Sanitation
entries.why: Chikkodi (in Belagavi) is largely rural, possibly lacking sanitation. We found no evidence tying sanitation to dropouts in Chikkodi specifically, but poor home sanitation can lead to illness and missed school.
entries.mechanism: Poor sanitation -> illness/menstrual hygiene issues -> irregular attendance -> dropout (general).

proof.quote: lost opportunities for education and work
girls’ school attendance is particularly boosted

entries.why: Belagavi has a mix of language communities (Kannada, Marathi) and no clear link between English-medium schools and dropouts was found. Local sources do not mention language as a cause of dropout.
entries.mechanism: Teaching in a non-native language can cause comprehension difficulties and dropout (general).

entries.why: Chikkodi schools mostly follow Kannada or Marathi medium. We found no evidence that English-medium instruction is causing dropouts here.
entries.mechanism: Classes in English can be hard for students not fluent in English, leading to dropout (general).

dominantFactorWhy.gaps: No Belagavi-specific data was found linking sanitation or medium of instruction to dropouts. District reports and news on dropout factors are lacking.

changes.summary: Rain damaged 1,901 government school buildings in Belagavi district in 2024, the most in Karnataka; the report calls them unsafe for students though not dilapidated. Older flood-hit and mixed-condition schools also show gaps.

findings.claim: Rain damaged 1,901 government school buildings in Belagavi district in 2024, the most in Karnataka; the report says they are unsafe for students though not dilapidated.
A Savadatti taluk government school in Belagavi district has only 10 of 22 rooms in good condition; an NGO began building 4 classrooms there in 2026.
findings.quote: The school has 4 buildings with 22 rooms out of which only 10 rooms are in good condition.

findings.claim: After the August 2019 floods a Kagawad taluk school in Belagavi district was left with only 3 usable classrooms; government and an NGO then built new ones.
findings.quote: All classrooms in the school have gone bad after the floods. 3 classrooms are in a usable condition.

changes.factor: % Schools with Furniture available for students
changes.summary: Only one older NGO project page found: a Belagavi district school in Athani taluk needed benches and desks along with new classrooms (completed 2016).

findings.claim: A Belagavi district school in Athani taluk needed new classrooms plus benches and desks for students; an NGO co-funded 7 new classrooms, completed in 2016.
findings.quote: The school needed new school structure complete with new classrooms and benches and desks for students.

changes.summary: Sources are indirect: a district youth-opportunity profile shows 35.6% of young women aged 15 to 21 out of education, and a 2017 study found gender disparities in Belagavi narrowing only slowly.

findings.claim: In Belagavi, 35.6% of young women aged 15 to 21 are out of education, about the same as the typical district.
findings.quote: 35.6% of young women aged 15 to 21 are out of education, close to the typical district.

findings.claim: A 2017 study of Belagavi district reported that gender disparities narrowed between 2001 and 2011, but only very slowly.
findings.quote: there is reduction in gender disparities from 2001 to 2011 but the reduction rate is very slow
